resources.string: The tablet is on a new Wi-Fi network. In the system dialog on screen, choose \"Allow\" and \"Always allow\".
Setup is not finished. In Settings, choose \"Run the setup wizard again\".
Wireless debugging could not be turned on. Check Wi-Fi is on and Samsung Auto Blocker is off, then tap Retry.
The tablet lost its wireless debugging pairing. In Settings, choose \"Run the setup wizard again\" and repeat the pairing step.
The keyboard link did not start. Tap Retry; if that does not help, restart the tablet.
The keyboard link keeps closing. Restart the tablet; if that does not help, tap Retry.

When off, the keyboard stays on the tablet
The PC no longer knows this tablet
%1$s on screen · Alt+Tab, Win and Ctrl+Alt+Del go to the PC too
Open %1$s and keys go to the PC by themselves
Open a new QR code on the PC and scan it from the PCs screen
The PC cannot type keys right now (for example a Windows security screen is open). The keyboard stays on the tablet meanwhile; keys go again once the PC is ready.
open · keys go to the PC
No paired PC yet. Scan the QR code shown by KeyRelay on Windows.
Ways to reach it · the top one is tried first
PC identity code · must match the one on the PC
You will need to pair it again to use it.
The PC could not be removed. Try again.
Show keys sent to the PC
Resume with %1$s · the keyboard stays on the tablet
Connecting… · %1$s · setting up a secure link
Keys go to the PC while this app is open
Continue only if you opened this QR code on your own PC.
The PC did not accept the code. Open a new QR code and try again.
Could not reach the PC. Check the PC is on and KeyRelay is running; away from home, access from outside must be on at the PC.
The PC\'s security ID does not match this QR code. Open a new QR code on the PC.
The pairing could not be saved on this tablet. Open a new QR code on the PC and try again.
This is not a KeyRelay QR code.
KeyRelay uses Android\'s \"Wireless debugging\" feature to pass the keyboard to the PC. You turn it on once; no computer needed.
If they are off: Settings → About tablet → Software information → Build number × 7
If Auto Blocker is on, it cuts wireless debugging and KeyRelay cannot start. Open the security settings with the button below and turn Auto Blocker off.
In Settings, tap \"Wireless debugging → Pair device with pairing code\". KeyRelay finds the rest itself; type only the 6-digit code here or in the notification.
Keep the pairing dialog open next to KeyRelay (split screen) or use the notification
The pairing dialog has not been found yet
The code was not accepted. Try again with a new code.
The code was wrong or the pairing dialog closed. Try again with a new code.
Paired, but wireless debugging could not be reached. Keep it on and try again.
Paired, but the permission was not granted. Try again.
Type the code from the notification
While the pairing dialog covers KeyRelay, you can type the code in a notification. That needs notification permission.
No notification permission. Type the code in the boxes above.
Type the code shown by Wireless debugging
In KeyRelay on Windows, open \"Pair\" and scan the QR code. The connection is encrypted; only your PC can read it.
KeyRelay starts by itself when the tablet starts. While %1$s is in front, every shortcut works on the PC.
Developer options and USB debugging stay on. Wireless debugging is on only for a moment while starting, then off again (also if you had turned it on).
How often the app checks the PC is still there
Without an answer in this time, the keyboard returns to the tablet
If a key does not reach the PC in this time, the connection counts as lost
Ctrl Alt and this key turn sending keys to the PC on and off. While it is off, Ctrl Alt Space also switches the Samsung keyboard language.
Same as the eye on the status screen. When off, which key you pressed never reaches the app screen.
While keys go to the PC, they do not type on the tablet

Turns the tablet keyboard typing on the PC on and off. On: while the app you chose is on screen, the keys you press go to the PC. Off: the keyboard always types on the tablet; if keys do not reach the PC, check this is on first.

Shows how many milliseconds a key takes to reach the PC and its answer to come back; the line draws the latest measurements. \"—\" means the tablet is not connected to the PC. If typing feels slow and the number is higher than usual, check your Wi-Fi or move to the PC\'s network.

Shows which app sends your keys to the PC while it is on screen. \"Open\": the app is on screen and your keys go to the PC. \"Closed or in the background\": the keyboard types on the tablet; open the app and keys switch to the PC by themselves.

Here you choose which app sends your keys to the PC while it is on screen (usually TeamViewer). In apps you did not choose, the keyboard types on the tablet. If you cannot find the app in the list, make sure it is installed on the tablet.

Shows which address the tablet is connected to the PC through; the connection is encrypted and the tablet connects only to the PC you paired. \"—\" means the tablet is not connected: check the PC is on and KeyRelay is running.

Shows the keys that turn sending to the PC on and off without touching the app: Ctrl + Alt + the key shown. Use it when you need to type something short on the tablet. If it clashes with something, pick another key in Settings.

Shows this PC\'s short identity code. While pairing it must match the code on the PC screen; if it does, you are connecting to the right PC. If not, do not pair; open a new QR code on the PC and try again.
Shows this PC\'s full security ID. You do not need it day to day; if support asks for it, read it here.

Shows the ways the tablet tries, in order, to reach the PC. \"Same network\" is used on your home or office Wi-Fi, \"Over the internet\" when you are away. If it does not connect while you are away and there is no \"Over the internet\" entry, turn on access from outside on the PC and pair again.

Decides how often the connection between the tablet and the PC is checked and when it counts as lost. Normally leave them. If the keyboard often returns to the tablet on a weak network, make them longer; if it returns late after the PC shuts down, make them shorter.
Shows the physical keyboards connected to the tablet right now. If you see \"No keyboard found\", check the keyboard is on and connected to the tablet over Bluetooth.
Chooses whether the status screen shows the last key sent to the PC. On: you see your keys really arrive. Off (default): which key you pressed never reaches the app.

The Android setting you turn on in this step: KeyRelay uses \"Wireless debugging\" only for a moment while starting, to hold the keyboard; no computer or cable needed. If KeyRelay later says \"Could not start\", check developer options are still on and Samsung Auto Blocker is off.

Your keyboard stays connected to the tablet; while %1$s is on screen the keys you press go to the PC, and in other apps it types on the tablet again. Need to type on the tablet in between? Toggle with %2$s. Tap ⓘ wherever you get stuck.
